# Make-up Exam for the First Midterm 1c 2022 – Types, types, types…

## Make-up of the 1st Midterm: Types, types, types…

A new developer implemented the functionality needed to determine, at the moment of importing a Customer (method `importCustomer` of `CustomerImporter`), whether the identification type is DNI or CUIT, with their corresponding validations.

He did the same at the moment of importing an Address (method `importAddress` of `CustomerImporter`), with the goal of being able to tell the old postal code (only 4 digits, e.g. 1636) from the new postal code (e.g. B1336BBE).

Because of these document types and postal code types, he added methods to `Customer` and `Address` to tell them apart.

Luckily there are tests for everything new. However, it seems he was unaware of good design practices and used IF in places where he could have used polymorphism, and he also left quite a lot of repeated code.

Your task is to remove the IFs and the repeated code you consider necessary in order to leave a good design. Any design and implementation change you consider necessary can be made, but the tests have to be kept as they are.

Use the Gradle project in the current directory (package `customerimporter`) as the starting point.

Work in the Gradle project in the current directory; it is the only place your work is read from. The code is in src/main/java/customerimporter and the tests in src/test/java/customerimporter, both in the package customerimporter. Run the tests with `gradle test` (Gradle is on the PATH). Do not create files outside this project.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. content.text:
I replaced the `if`s that decided between types with polymorphism and removed the repeated code. All 29 tests pass (`gradle test`, 0 failures) and `ImportTest.java` is unchanged.

## New classes
- **`Identification`** (abstract), with subclasses **`DNI`** and **`CUIT`**
  - `Identification.of(type, number)` finds the right subclass in a map from type code to constructor (`"D"` → `DNI`, `"C"` → `CUIT`). An unknown code throws "Invalid identification type", so there's no `if/else if/else` left.
  - Each subclass checks its own number in its constructor. The "if the condition fails, throw this message" line that was written out many times now lives in one method, `assertValidNumber`, and each subclass supplies its own error message.
  - Each subclass answers `isDNI`/`isCUIT`, `dniNumberIfNone`/`cuitNumberIfNone` and `type` itself, so the `if (hasXxx) ... else aNoneBlock` checks are gone.
- **`ZipCode`** (abstract), with subclasses **`OldZipCode`** (stores an `int`) and **`NewZipCode`** (stores a `String`)
  - `ZipCode.from(aString)` picks the subclass by the first character (digit → old, letter → new) from a list of kinds. If neither matches, it throws the same message as before.
  - The subclasses handle `isOld`/`isNew`, `oldZipCodeIfNone`/`newZipCodeIfNone` and `value()`. This removes the `instanceof Integer` / `instanceof String` checks and the zip code held as a plain `Object`.
- **`Characters`**: holds `areAllDigits` / `areAllLetters`, which replace the `chars().allMatch(...)` code that was copied five times.

## Changes to existing classes
- **`Customer`** now holds an `Identification` instead of two strings and passes its calls on to it. It also has a new `isIdentifiedAs(type, number)`.
- **`Address`** now holds a `ZipCode` and passes its calls on to it. `zipCode()` still returns the raw value (the `Integer` or `String`), because the tests compare against those values directly.
- **`TransientCustomerSystem` / `PersistentCustomerSystem`**: both had their own copy of the customer lookup condition; they now call `aCustomer.isIdentifiedAs(...)`.
- **`CustomerImporter`**:
  - `importCustomer` and `importAddress` just read the fields and delegate to `Identification.of` and `ZipCode.from`.
  - I also replaced the record-type `if` chain in `importRecord` with a map (`"C"` → `importCustomer`, `"A"` → `importAddress`) and removed `isCustomerRecord`/`isAddressRecord`, which nothing used anymore. The exam didn't ask for this change.

A few checks with `if` remain: the record size checks, "customer was imported", "record is not empty", and the two new one-line assert methods. They check that the input is valid rather than choosing between types, so I left them.

The tests pin one oddity: an invalid zip code still gives the message "Invalid identification type". It's defined once, in `ZipCode.invalidZipCodeTypeErrorDescription()`.
